item.title: EU Accepts Meta’s Updated Ad Model for January 2026 Rollout
item.description: EU regulators have accepted Meta’s revised advertising model for Facebook and Instagram, with the company set to present the new options to users in January 2026. The decision removes the immediate risk of daily fines under the Digital Markets Act (DMA). The updated pay-or-consent model introduces two choices. item.title: The New Era of Mobile App Deception
item.description: Retail apps now process their highest transaction volumes during peak periods. item.title: Pew Survey: 64% of Teens Use AI Chatbots, and 97% Go Online Daily
item.description: A new Pew Research Center survey of 1,458 U.S. teens shows how central digital platforms and AI tools have become in their daily lives. Nearly all teens (97 percent to be exact) go online each day, and four in ten say they are online almost constantly. Older teens report higher levels of constant use than younger teens, and rates are even higher among Black and Hispanic teens. item.title: Research Tracks 8,324 U.S. Children, Identifying Social Media as a Risk Factor for Growing Inattention
item.description: A longitudinal study, published in Pediatrics Open Science, following 8,324 children aged 9 to 14 in the United States has found that social media use is associated with a gradual increase in inattention symptoms. item.title: Studies Reveal Severe Gen Z Burnout and Recommend Stronger Workplace Support and Clearer Expectations
item.description: Gen Z workers are reporting some of the highest burnout levels ever recorded, with new research suggesting they are buckling under unprecedented levels of stress. While people of all age levels report burnout, Gen Z and millennials are reporting “peak burnout” at earlier ages. In the United States, a poll of 2,000 adults found that a quarter of Americans are burnt out before they’re 30 years old.
